title: daily-scratchpad-gpu-ops-11
content:
Daily scratchpad - GPU ops (quick notes / todo)

2026-03-04 morning check-in:
- quick health sweep of dedicated pools (us-west-2a / eu-central-1): no immediate OOMs reported, avg token latency +3% last 24h
- alerts: node-gpu-14 flapping NVLINK error ~03:40 UTC (filed JIRA-4521)
- capacity forecast: Dedicated customer X will increase baseline qps by ~20% starting 2026-03-10 (follow up w/ sales for commit)

Top priorities:
1) NVLINK flapping on node-gpu-14 (high)
   - repro steps: stress 80% mem + multi-GPU attention kernel -> link errors after ~30m
   - temporary mitigation: pin workloads to single-GPU variant for affected tenant (route in policy)
   - long-term: schedule node for firmware + driver update, check motherboard BIOS (blocked on maintenance window)
2) Prepare capacity bump for Dedicated X (medium-high)
   - checklist: reserve 4 x A100-80GB (or equivalent q8_0 quantized profile), add to pool, pre-warm cache
   - coordination: infra procurement (Priya), sales + account exec (Jordan) to confirm start date
3) Kernel upgrade for inference runtime on canary cluster (medium)
   - target: bump to linux-5.19 + nvidia-driver 530.x
   - smoke tests: perf regression on 16k token long prompt, KV cache correctness, latency SLO 95th < 250ms for small chat model

Routine todo (today):
- [ ] Reboot node-gpu-14 into maintenance mode, capture dmesg and nvlink logs (owner: Avery) -- prefer 03:00-05:00 PT window
- [ ] Open ticket with vendor for NVLINK telemetry export (attach logs) (owner: Avery)
- [ ] Add Dedicated X to capacity plan spreadsheet (link above) + update cost forecast for q2 (30m)
- [ ] Run pre-upgrade perf run on canary cluster (run perf harness, compare to baseline) (owner: Jordan)
- [ ] Validate autoscaler headroom after adding reserved GPUs (simulate 2x burst)
- [ ] Confirm backup snapshot policy for /var/kvcache before rolling changes

Notes to self / random ideas:
- consider MIG-like partitioning for A100-80GB for small-embedding workloads to improve packing; need to test latency tail impact
- caching: can we warm prefix cache using synthetic traces for Dedicated X to reduce cold-start tokens? sketch pipeline: replay recent 7d queries -> warm caches in pre-warm window
- explore compress-on-wire for KV snapshots to reduce snapshot time (gzip vs zstd)

Blocked / dependency list:
- maintenance window approval from compliance for EU regions (waiting on security advisory)
- vendor firmware for NVLINK stability (ticket pending)

Meeting notes (infra sync 2026-03-03):
- decided to push kernel upgrade to canary only this week, broad rollout next week if perf stable
- SRE to add specific alert for nvlink_retries > 10 in 15m window (owner: Priya)
- Ops playbook update: add checklist for multi-gpu jobs fallback to single-gpu variant if nvlink errors detected

Quick commands / snippets to run:
- collect logs from node: sudo journalctl -u nvidia-driver -S "-1h" > /tmp/nvlink-logs.txt
- capture nvlink status: nvidia-smi nvlink --status
- perf harness: ./infra/tools/perf/run.sh --config canary-16k --repeat 3 --output /tmp/perf-canary.json

End-of-day 2026-03-04:
- progress: opened vendor ticket, added Dedicated X to capacity spreadsheet, scheduled maintenance tentative 2026-03-06 03:00 PT (pending approvals)
- follow-ups for tomorrow: merge autoscaler headroom test results, run canary perf, confirm maintenance approvals

Misc: rough time estimates for items
- NVLINK firmware + reboot + verification: ~2h (if vendor patch available)
- Capacity add + pre-warm: ~3-4h coordination + provisioning time
- Kernel upgrade canary run: 1-2h + 1h analysis

---
Small personal note: remember to sync with product-hosted-api on rollout policy changes; need to ensure fallback route config is compatible with canary model variants.
